# Authoring AGENTS.md

Write the instruction file a future coding agent reads first. The file must
carry hard constraints, commands, layout, and standing conventions — not a
task backlog, not a restated README.

## When to Use

Use when asked to create, extend, or restructure a repo's `AGENTS.md` (or an
equivalent agent instruction file such as `CLAUDE.md`/`.cursorrules`) for a
project that has none or a stale one.

## Procedure

1. **Inspect the repo before writing a word.** Read `package.json`/manifest
   (scripts, engines), `README.md`, and the `docs/` tree — especially ADRs and
   requirement specs, which contain the real hard constraints. List the layout
   (`find . -type f -not -path './node_modules/*' -not -path './.git/*'`).
   Every rule in the file must trace to a repo file or to the user's words —
   never invent a constraint to sound thorough (a fabricated budget or ban
   misleads later work).
2. **Name the hard constraints** the agent must never break: size budgets,
   zero-dependency rules, 'no engine', banned APIs (`Math.random()` for world
   content), enforced checks. Cite the ADR or script that enforces each.
3. **Draft with the sections in this order:** what the project is → hard
   constraints → commands (start / test / pre-completion check) → layout →
   workflow rules → communication. One page. Point to `docs/` for depth instead
   of restating it — the file duplicates docs it drifts from.
4. **Encode only always-on rules.** No task descriptions or work items; a
   specific task list belongs in the task docs, not the standing instructions.
5. **Ask the user which conventions to encode** when they are not already
   stated: TDD gates (red/green), where plans/design docs are saved for
   traceability, communication style. Include each as a one-shot imperative
   rule, not a narrative of how the user said it.
6. **Write as `AGENTS.md` at repo root.** Later edits are `patch`-edits to the
   section that changed, never a full rewrite — the file accumulates user
   decisions each of which must survive.
7. **Commit only when asked** (check `git status` first; the distro-snapped
   workspace block goes stale). If the identity is unset, recover per the
   `github` skill (its `references/pr-workflow.md`): take the identity from
   the repo's existing history and set it repo-locally.

## Pitfalls

- An empty traceability folder (e.g. `docs/plans/`) does not survive git —
  create the folder with its first plan file, or ship a README placeholder.
- Keep phrase-level wording for preference rules ('for dummies' style,
  'ask before'), not a paraphrase — the tone the user asked for is the
  requirement itself.

{"content": "1|# AGENTS.md — FairFahren
2|
3|Rules for AI coding agents working in this repo.
4|
5|## What this project is
6|
7|A procedural 3D driving game (steer a German taxi through a generated slice of
8|Berlin) built as a base project for developer interviews. Candidates extend it.
9|
10|- **~52 KB of plain JavaScript. No assets, no dependencies, no build step.**
11|- Everything is generated from one seed (`?seed=42` gives the same city to everyone).
12|- Requires Node 22+ and a browser with WebGL2.
13|
14|## Hard constraints (never break these)
15|
16|1. **Zero dependencies** — nothing goes in `package.json` dependencies, no `node_modules`.
17|2. **Raw WebGL2, no engine** — no three.js/Babylon or any 3D library (ADR 0001).
18|3. **No asset files** — all content is generated from a seed; surface detail comes
19|   from the fragment shader. `Math.random()` is banned for world content — use the
20|   seeded RNG (`src/core/rng.js`) with **forked streams** (`rng.fork('…')`) so one
21|   feature doesn't reshuffle the rest of the world.
22|4. **Size budget is enforced** — `npm run size` fails above **96 KB raw / 32 KB gzip**
23|   for `index.html` + `src/**`. Source ships unminified and readable; every byte counts.
24|5. **Generation is plain data** — `generateCity` produces data that is separately
25|   turned into geometry (`buildCityMesh`) and colliders, so it stays testable in Node.
26|
27|## Commands
28|
29|```bash
30|npm start        # dev server on http://localhost:8080
31|npm test         # node --test unit tests
32|npm run size     # size budget check
33|npm run check    # tests + size check — run this before considering work done
34|```
35|
36|## Layout
37|
38|```
39|index.html            page, HUD, loads src/main.js
40|src/main.js           wiring + fixed-timestep game loop
41|src/core/             seeded RNG, math (matrices)
42|src/gfx/              mesh builder, shaders, WebGL2 renderer
43|src/world/            city generator (pure data) + city mesh
44|src/vehicle/          taxi physics, collision, taxi model
45|src/game/             input, camera, HUD
46|test/                 unit tests (node:test, *.test.mjs)
47|tools/                dev server, size check
48|docs/                 requirements, spec, candidate brief, ADRs
49|```
50|
51|Details live in `docs/01`–`04` and `docs/adr/`. Read them when a task touches
52|requirements, rendering, generation, or the size budget.
53|
54|## Workflow rules
55|
56|**Traceability:** all plans, working documents, and design decisions are saved
57|in a dedicated folder inside `docs/` (e.g. `docs/plans/`), never just in chat.
58|Plans go there automatically; anything else (notes, lists, stray docs) goes
59|there only after asking the user first.
60|
61|- **Red/green TDD is mandatory.** For every new behavior: first write a failing
62|  test (red), watch it fail for the expected reason, then write the smallest code
63|  that makes it pass (green), then clean up. Never write implementation before
64|  its failing test; never ship with `npm run check` failing.
65|- Tests run in Node with `node:test` — keep game logic (world gen, physics, RNG)
66|  pure and browser-free so it stays testable.
67|- Match the existing style: ES modules, plain functions over classes, small
68|  commented code.
69|- Don't commit, push, or rewrite history unless explicitly asked.
70|
71|## Communication
72|
73|- When the user asks questions, answer **"for dummies" style**: plain language,
74|  short sentences, everyday analogies, no jargon without a one-line explanation.", "total_lines": 74, "file_size": 3355, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false, "not_found": false}

Done. AGENTS.md's workflow rules now read:

- **Removed** the mandatory red/green TDD bullet.
- **Added** "Speed over ceremony" in its place — smallest working change fast, no test-first gates. The safety net stays: `npm run check` must still pass before work counts as done.
- **Added** "Deploy review agents if needed" — for big, risky, or constraint-touching changes, spin up review agent(s) to check the diff before finishing.

The traceability, style, and "don't commit unless asked" rules are untouched. It's a docs-only change, so no tests or size check were affected.
